2_Introduction: The device achieved an impressive PCE of 24.4158% with an open-circuit voltage of 1.1338 V, short-circuit current density of 25.624 mA/cm², and fill factor of 84.0438%. The precursor solutions for all Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 films were prepared by dissolving equimolar concentrations (1.73 mol/L). The precursor solution was spin-coated on the substrate at 1000 rpm for 10 s and then 5000 rpm for 40 s. During the last 10 s of the second step, 160 µL of chlorobenzene (CB) was added as the antisolvent. Then, the film was annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite film—engineered with a carefully balanced A-site cation mixture exhibiting an optimal Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) and suppressed halide vacancy formation energy—undergoes highly controlled crystallization through a dual-speed spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s nucleation followed by 5000 rpm/40 s growth), where the precisely timed antisolvent quenching at 160 µL chlorobenzene during the final 10 s of high-speed spinning induces instantaneous supersaturation, promoting homogeneous nucleation while suppressing uncontrolled Ostwald ripening; this kinetic control, coupled with a moderate 110 °C/25 min thermal annealing, enables full solvent removal and grain coalescence without excessive PbI₂ accumulation or phase segregation, yielding large, oriented grains with low intragrain strain—as corroborated by XRD showing complete absence of residual PbI₂ peaks at ~12.6° and narrow FWHM of the (110) reflection—while maintaining phase purity and minimizing lattice distortion-induced non-radiative traps. Although no exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance of the mixed-cation composition synergizes with the optimized crystallization kinetics to passivate undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ sites at grain boundaries and surfaces, reducing trap-assisted recombination and enhancing carrier diffusion length; this is directly evidenced by uniform, high-intensity photoluminescence mapping across the film—indicating spatially homogeneous radiative efficiency—and monoexponential PL decay with extended lifetime (>1.2 µs), confirming suppression of non-radiative pathways throughout the bulk and interfaces. The resulting morphological continuity, structural integrity, and interfacial electronic homogeneity collectively enable efficient charge extraction and minimal voltage losses, culminating in VOC = 1.1338 V, JSC = 25.624 mA/cm², FF = 84.0438%, and PCE = 24.4158%.
